Generated by scripts/build_entity_resolution_fixtures.py (which reuses export_fixtures.py's build_case()) against a synthetic document, specifically for Phase 6 (EntityResolutionEngine). Covers candidate/occurrence/quality/entity-group/ambiguity output (architecture v0.2 §13.1, Domain Parity Fixtures). Interaction and performance fixtures are tracked separately -- see fixtures/interaction/ and fixtures/performance/, both currently empty.

Deliberately exercises, and confirms via the real Python oracle (not hand-predicted):
1. Variant-name grouping via the first-name bucket mechanism: 'Maria Alvarez' (a merged candidate -- see point 4) plus a repeated bare 'Maria' short reference group into one entity ('person:alvarez:m'), confidence 46 (the bare short reference pulls the group's min-based confidence down). SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28 -- see deviations[] below: this was actually the same silent-auto-merge defect the ambiguity-anchor correction fixed, caught retroactively by this very fixture.
2. Two same-first-name people, each given a same-initial second variant ('Andrew Goodloe'/'Andy Goodloe', 'Andrew Jackson'/'Andy Jackson') so each forms a real 2-member group, plus a repeated bare 'Andrew' that becomes AMBIGUOUS between both groups (person:jackson:a confidence 91, person:goodloe:a confidence 86) -- directly modeled on tests/test_entity_resolution.py's own ambiguity test shape.
3. Same-surname-different-first-initial pair ('Carlos Mendez' / 'Elena Mendez') that must NOT merge -- confirmed: no group ever contains both, since entity-resolution's group key is last-name + FIRST-INITIAL, not last-name alone.
4. CONFIRMED PYTHON QUIRK, not a TS deviation: 'Dr Susan Whitmore' (title with no period, so detectors.py's FALLBACK_PERSON_RE sweeps the title into the candidate text as a 3rd token) and plain 'Susan Whitmore' elsewhere do NOT merge into the same entity-resolution group, because _person_group_key() uses the candidate's FIRST token as the group's initial -- 'dr' for the titled form, 'susan' for the plain form -- producing different group keys ('person:whitmore:d' vs 'person:whitmore:s') even though a human reviewer would recognize both as the same Susan Whitmore. A real, product-relevant finding: title prefixes (when not followed by a period) silently prevent entity-resolution grouping. Ported faithfully, not silently corrected during migration -- see docs/detection/phase-6-findings.md.
5. 'Priya Natarajan' is a singleton (appears once, no variant anywhere) and correctly forms no group and no ambiguity proposal.
6. 'Alvarez, Maria' (comma-form) and 'Maria Alvarez' (plain form) are pre-merged into ONE candidate by DETECTION's own normalize_candidate() (Phase 4) before entity-resolution ever runs -- confirming 'Last, First vs First Last' variant-matching is NOT entity-resolution's job in this pipeline, despite superficially looking like a grouping concern.

deviations.reason: Andrew traced a real document where a bare first name ('Andrew') sharing a token with a full-name entity that had only ONE detected spelling ('Andrew Goodloe') was never proposed as an ambiguity -- see src/engines/entity-resolution/resolution.ts's top doc comment ("DISCLOSED BEHAVIORAL CHANGE") and docs/detection/ambiguity-anchor-correction.md for the full trace. This fixture's own 'Maria'/'Maria Alvarez' pairing (note 1 above) turns out to be the SAME defect: Python's build_entity_groups() silently auto-merged the bare 'Maria' short reference into 'Maria Alvarez''s bucket with no reviewer confirmation, because exactly one full-name bucket matched. The corrected TS implementation no longer performs that silent merge, so 'person:alvarez:m' no longer reaches entity-groups.json's >=2-member threshold on its own and is correctly demoted from a realized group to a solitary ambiguity anchor -- 'Maria' is now proposed to the reviewer via Ambiguity Check instead ('ts groups: 2' vs Python's 'expected groups: 3'; 'ts ambiguous: 2' [Andrew + Maria] vs Python's 'expected ambiguous: 1' [Andrew only]). This is a deliberate, disclosed non-parity correction of a genuine Python-oracle defect, not an accidental TS regression -- Python's own build_entity_groups()/build_ambiguous_matches() were not modified (and could not be, per this migration's read-only-oracle constraint), so this fixture's expected/entity-groups.json and expected/ambiguity-proposals.json still capture the ORIGINAL buggy Python output on purpose, as a historical record of the defect this fixture inadvertently also exercises. verify/entity-resolution-parity.ts treats this exact divergence, for this fixture only, as an approved deviation rather than a failure.
